definitions.explanation: A mark or discoloration on fabric or other surfaces.
Spots or marks on the skin, especially from sun exposure or aging.

examples.japanese: シャツに{染|し}みがついた。
examples.english: I got a stain on my shirt.

examples.japanese: コーヒーの{染|し}みがなかなか{落|お}ちなくて{困|こま}っている。
examples.english: I'm having trouble getting the coffee stain out.
I got blemishes on my face.

examples.japanese: {日焼|ひや}け{止|ど}めを{塗|ぬ}らないとシミができやすい。
examples.english: If you don't apply sunscreen, you'll easily get age spots.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{取|と}ると{手|て}の{甲|こう}にもシミが{出|で}てくることがある。
examples.english: As you get older, age spots can appear on the backs of your hands too.

notes:
{染|し}み has two main meanings: stains on fabric or surfaces, and blemishes or age spots on skin. The word covers any kind of discoloration that shouldn't be there.

COMMON PATTERNS (fabric):
- {染|し}みがつく: to get a stain
- {染|し}みを{落|お}とす: to remove a stain
- {染|し}み{抜|ぬ}き: stain removal
- {血|ち}の{染|し}み: bloodstain

SKIN USAGE:
- シミができる: to develop age spots
- シミ{対策|たいさく}: anti-blemish measures
- シミそばかす: spots and freckles

WRITING:
When referring to skin blemishes, シミ is commonly written in katakana, especially in cosmetics and skincare contexts. For fabric stains, both {染|し}み and しみ are used.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {染|し}み: stain, blemish (discoloration)
- {汚|よご}れ: dirt, grime (general uncleanliness)
- {傷|きず}: scratch, flaw (physical damage)
